newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: World Bank seeks Argentine jobs flexibility - report.
newsitem.headline: World Bank seeks Argentine jobs flexibility - report.

text.p: The World Bank deems an agreement on labor reform between the Argentine government and unions made good progress but thinks more flexibility is needed, a top bank's official was quoted Tuesday as saying.

The agreement reached Friday made "tremendous progress," the bank's Argentine representative Patricio Millan said according to Clarin newspaper. Nevertheless it must not be considered definitive but a step in the right direction and should be completed "with more progress on flexibility," Millan added.
Businessmen have balked at the agreement, saying it allows unions too many privileges.
Peronist President Carlos Menem's government considers labor reform as crucial to bringing down unemployment, that has skyrocketed to 17.3 percent.
